units.translation: 258 ff. Verse 258 has been turned into a bad trimeter: ⟦1⟧ (cf. below, 266); Hermann deleted the inappropriate ⟦2⟧. But one must write ⟦3⟧, since ⟦4⟧ in Aeschylus is hardly found otherwise than with d' before it, 49 (⟦5⟧'). ⟦6⟧ (at 410 I have, with Wilamowitz, written ⟦7⟧ = ⟦8⟧). 980 etc. For ⟦9⟧, ⟦10⟧ (Scaliger, Wakefield) is correct, if above ⟦11⟧ is correctly explained. That the scholiast does not unconditionally testify for ⟦12⟧ (⟦13⟧), Hermann notes, in that, if ⟦14⟧ refers to ⟦15⟧, ⟦16⟧ is passed over, and this word is explained by Hesychius with ⟦17⟧, ⟦18⟧, ⟦19⟧. 261-263. The words refuse to fit into a construction, since ⟦20⟧ is subject and ⟦21⟧ also is; furthermore ⟦22⟧ and ⟦23⟧ are the same. Schol.: ⟦24⟧ (i.e. ⟦25⟧, with which the ancients explain) ⟦26⟧· ⟦27⟧. So period (Hermann) after ⟦28⟧ (and new speaker?), so that ⟦29⟧ is the entire predicate, = ⟦30⟧ or ⟦31⟧. The cry of woe ⟦32⟧ is of course directed at the doer; to ⟦33⟧. Wecklein compares ⟦34⟧ ⟦35⟧; ⟦36⟧ like ⟦37⟧; on ⟦38⟧ see on ⟦39⟧. (Wecklein takes ⟦40⟧ as relative, which in itself would be permissible, but makes ⟦41⟧ the predicate, so that ⟦42⟧ becomes part of the relative clause; that is an impossible position, and the combination ⟦43⟧ would have to be understood as article and substantivized adjective.) 264-268. ⟦44⟧ libation like ⟦45⟧. ⟦46⟧ (-⟦47⟧) ⟦48⟧ (manuscripts) looks like a begun trimeter (on 258), which would have become complete with ⟦49⟧; but the Doric forms point to lyric rhythm, which one obtains by ⟦50⟧ (Wellauer): dochmius with cretic dimeter as at 268 cretic dimeter with dochmius. For the expression cf. ⟦51⟧: ⟦52⟧, ⟦53⟧. After 266 one can (Hermann) let the speaker(s) change. On 267 cf. 305 ⟦54⟧, 302 ⟦55⟧ (3) ⟦56⟧; already alive he becomes instead of a ⟦57⟧ dry like the dead, who ⟦58⟧, and so finally enters the underworld. ⟦59⟧ very good Schütz for ⟦60⟧ (⟦61⟧ ⟦62⟧); ⟦63⟧ for -ous already Casaubon.
this man again, at any rate, having strength around the image
in return for which he owes us, the suppliant wishes to become the goddess's
poured out upon the earth, hard to gather up
who could call it back again
on the ground, on the ground
may I carry off as food
of a drink hard to drink
may I carry off as food
and you will feast on me while living
